title: fix(console): settings icons go through getLazyIcon's known-name check (objectui#11679)
body:
Fixes #11679

Clause-②: no

The claim's line was `yes`; the seat amended it to `no` on objectui#11679 (claim amendment), on this measured reading: no export is added to or removed from any package entry. After the build, `packages/app-shell/dist/index.d.ts` names no `getIcon` (0 hits; control `readEnvelopeFailureText`: 1 hit). The package's `exports` map has only `.`. The helper the console now calls, `getLazyIcon`, was already exported by `@object-ui/components` before this branch. The changeset stays `minor` (the seat's answer to this PR's open question): published app-shell chrome changes what it renders for a digit-suffixed name.

## What was wrong

- The console's own `getIcon` (`apps/console/src/utils/getIcon.ts`, now deleted) handed every name to lucide's `DynamicIcon` without a known-name check.
- **The unknown name is `Building2`.** It is the `icon` of the framework's company settings manifest: objectstack `packages/services/service-settings/src/manifests/company.manifest.ts`, symbol `companySettingsManifest`, key `icon` (read at objectstack `f76c6221`). `Building2` is a real Lucide icon, the PascalCase export of `building-2`. The console copy's tokeniser lacked the letter-to-digit boundary that objectui#9414 gave `toKebabIconName`, so it produced `building2`, which Lucide does not have. `DynamicIcon` then called `console.error` with the card's message from its effect, and drew its fallback bare, without the page's classes. The console mounts under `React.StrictMode`, which runs effects twice in development; that matches the card's "twice".
- Every other icon name the framework's settings manifests declare at `f76c6221` tokenises to a Lucide name under both the old and the new tokeniser. `Building2` is the only one that does not. This was probed against the installed lucide-react 1.43.0 `iconNames`, over `Timer`, `Sparkles`, `Plug`, `RotateCcw`, `LockKeyhole`, `Palette`, `Building2`, `FlaskConical`, `BookOpen`, `Globe`, `Mail`, `MessageSquare` and `HardDrive`.
- The producer is correct. The spec declares the manifest `icon` as "Optional Lucide icon name", and `Building2` is one. Nothing is filed against objectstack.

## The change

The order's suggested route was to reuse app-shell's helper. Measurement ruled that out: app-shell's `getIcon` checked the name before calling `DynamicIcon`, but used the same tokeniser. Reusing it would have silenced the error and drawn the `Database` glyph for the company settings, which is the objectui#9414 failure mode. `@object-ui/components` already exports `getLazyIcon`, which has both the known-name check and the digit boundary, and the console already depends on that package.

- `SettingsHub`, `SettingsView` and `SettingsField` call `getLazyIcon` from `@object-ui/components`, and the console copy is deleted. Their `react-hooks/static-components` disable comments now name `getLazyIcon`.
- App-shell's `utils/getIcon.ts` keeps its path and export name and re-exports `getLazyIcon`, so the two copies are one. At this head it has 16 importers, and 12 tests that `vi.mock` that path; none of them changes.
- **File surface extension, outside the claim:** `scripts/check-lucide-icon-record-names.mjs`. Its `DECLARED_DYNAMIC_READERS` census listed both retired copies, and `check:icon-record-names` reported both entries as STALE, with the instruction "Update the census — do not delete the gate". The two entries are removed, and `lazy-icon.tsx` stays listed. Any route that deletes the console copy breaks this gate, so the edit belongs to this card; the claim's file surface did not name it.
- Changeset: `.changeset/11679-console-settings-icons.md` (`@object-ui/console`, `@object-ui/app-shell`).

## Tests

New pins:

- `apps/console/src/pages/settings/__tests__/SettingsIcons.knownName-11679.test.tsx` runs against the real `./api` over a stubbed `fetch` and the real `getLazyIcon`. It has three tests. (1) An unknown name (`box-open`) on a hub card renders `lucide-database` with the call site's `h-6`, and `console.error` stays silent. (2) The same holds on a namespace page and its action button. (3) `Building2` renders `lucide-building-2` on the hub and on the company page, again with `console.error` silent. `console.warn` is filtered to lucide or icon-name mentions only, because the i18n layer warns there for every manifest namespace the bundle has no key for.
- `packages/app-shell/src/utils/__tests__/getIcon.oneHelper-11679.test.ts` has three tests: `getIcon` is `getLazyIcon` by identity; `getIcon('Building2')` is not `Database`; `getIcon('box-open')` is `Database`.

Final run at `537e8cc`, through the verify lock: `pnpm exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2` over the console settings directory, `AppContent.systemHubRoutes.test.tsx`, both new pins, `SearchResultsPage.records.test.tsx`, the 12 app-shell tests that mock `utils/getIcon`, and every test that names `check-lucide-icon-record-names`. Result: `Test Files  36 passed (36)`, `Tests  378 passed (378)`, exit 0.

**Ablation**, at `c5a3bb7`, through the verify lock. The pre-fix sources were put back from `da35453` into the worktree only, with the index untouched: the console helper, the three settings pages' imports, and app-shell's own copy. The run was guarded by a `trap` restore.

- Landing proof before the run: each settings page had 1 `utils/getIcon` import and 0 `getLazyIcon`; the resurrected console helper had 0 `VALID_ICON_NAMES`; app-shell's file had 0 re-exports and 1 own implementation.
- Mutated run: `Tests  5 failed | 1 passed (6)`. The namespace-page leg received `Error: [lucide-react]: Name in Lucide DynamicIcon not found` twice, which is the card's message. The `Building2` leg failed with `expected 'lucide lucide-database' to contain 'lucide-building-2'`. The hub leg failed with `expected 'lucide lucide-database' to contain 'h-6'`, which is the bare `DynamicIcon` fallback. The app-shell identity and `Building2` legs went red. The `box-open` app-shell leg stayed green as expected, because the old copy did check the name.
- Restore: `git diff HEAD` was 0 bytes and porcelain status 0 lines. All four tracked paths matched their HEAD blob hashes, and the resurrected file was absent. The restored run was `6 passed (6)`.
- Resolution path: vitest aliases `@object-ui/components` to `packages/components/src`, and the old console helper was a relative import. No `dist/` sits on either leg's path, so neither leg needed a rebuild.
- The two later commits do not touch a runtime subject. `ab5c1c1` types the console spies (`MockInstance`), and `537e8cc` changes only the gate script.

## Gates (head `537e8cc` unless noted)

- `turbo run build --filter='@object-ui/console^...' --concurrency=2`: 34/34 successful, at `c5a3bb7`. No package source has changed since.
- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/app-shell type-check`: 0. `pnpm --filter @object-ui/console type-check`: 0. App-shell's `tsconfig.test.json` lists the new pin (`--listFilesOnly`).
- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/app-shell lint`: 0 (0 errors). `pnpm --filter @object-ui/console lint`: 0 (0 errors). Both ran at `ab5c1c1`; `537e8cc` touches neither package.
- Root-scope lint of the edited script: `eslint --format json scripts/check-lucide-icon-record-names.mjs` gave 1 file, 0 errors, 0 warnings. This is a proven narrowing. (1) The population is `lint:root` in the root `package.json`, which lints `.` and ignores only `packages/*/**`, `examples/*/**`, `apps/*/**` and `docs/**`, so `scripts/` is in it. (2) The file count, 1, is read from the JSON output. (3) `eslint.config.js` sets no `parserOptions.project` or `projectService`, so linting is not type-aware and this diff cannot move the verdict of an untouched file.
- 0 exit: `check:icon-record-names` (`OK  lucide icon names: 187 authored/declared names reaching 1 record-reading resolver`), `check:self-import`, `check:unreferenced-sources`, `check:new-line-citations` (`0 new citation(s)`), `check:control-bytes`, `check:changeset-claims`, `check:pending-changeset-literals`, `check:entry-guard`, `check:docs-route-closure`, `check-changeset-no-major.mjs`, `check-changeset-presence.mjs` (`7 source file(s) of 2 released package(s) changed, and this change declares 1 changeset(s)`), `check-changeset-fixed.mjs`, and `check:readme-exports`. The first `check:readme-exports` run could not judge, because `@object-ui/cli` and `@object-ui/plugin-ai` were unbuilt; after building both it passed.
- 0 exit at `ab5c1c1`: `check:phantom-deps`, `check:unused-deps`, `check:test-path-roots`, `check:vi-mock-specifiers`, `check:vi-mock-inherit` and `check:vi-mock-override-shape`.
- `node scripts/check-governed-queue-guard.mjs --test` over the 9 paths: NOT GOVERNED.

NOT MEASURED, declared to CI:

- `check:eager-closure`. Reason: it reads `apps/console/dist/eager-closure.json`, which needs a full console `vite build`; `performance-budget.yml` builds it and runs the check. Expected direction, an inference that was not measured: the diff removes two `lucide-react/dynamic` imports (the console's and app-shell's own) and routes both through `lazy-icon.tsx`, which already imports that module.
- The full app-shell suite. Reason: proven narrowing with a stated blind spot. App-shell's `getIcon` changes behaviour only for a name with an unhyphenated letter-digit boundary. No canonical Lucide name carries one, so every name that resolved before still resolves the same; `lazy-icon-digit-boundary-9414.test.ts` re-derives that no-loss property. Of the 149 app-shell test files that import a `getIcon` importer, 12 mock the module, and one carries a digit-suffixed icon literal on an `icon` line (`SearchResultsPage.records.test.tsx`, `Building2`). That one was run and is green. The blind spot is an icon name that reaches a test through a fixture rather than as a literal on an `icon` line.

## Acceptance notes

- lucide-react 1.43.0's `DynamicIcon` renders its `fallback` with no props, so any caller that hands it an unchecked name draws a glyph without its classes. The known-name check makes that path unreachable through `getLazyIcon`. This is an observation and is not filed.
- `check:unreferenced-sources` does not cover `apps/console` or `packages/app-shell`, by its own output (`COVERED_PACKAGES`). Its green therefore says nothing about the deleted helper. `git grep` finds no importer of `utils/getIcon` left in `apps/console`.
